threats.title: Unauthorized download of another customer's export via leaked or guessable download link
threats.description: A malicious or compromised customer obtains the download link for another customer's export and uses it to download the export file if the link is not strongly bound to the authenticated requester.
preconditions: The Export API returns a download link to the customer over HTTPS when an export is ready, and that link can be used later to retrieve the file (established: the API returns a download link when the export is ready over a public HTTPS service; evd-001, evd-002).

Download links function as bearer tokens or are otherwise not strictly bound to the authenticated customer's identity and session (for example, a presigned or opaque URL with no additional authorization check).

An attacker acting as a customer can obtain or guess a download link issued for another customer's export (for example, via logs, misdirected communication, browser history, or weakly unguessable identifiers).
attack_path: A legitimate customer requests an export over the public HTTPS Export API and, once the export is assembled, receives a download link (evd-001, evd-002).
The export file containing that customer's records for the requested date range is written to the managed object store (evd-003).
The download link corresponding to that export is exposed to or guessed by a different, malicious customer.

The malicious customer uses their client to invoke the download link; if the system treats possession of the link as sufficient authorization, the Export API or storage layer serves the export file for the other customer, disclosing their records.
threats.impact: Confidential customer records for another tenant are disclosed via the export file, breaching cross-customer isolation and exposing a full, time-bounded dataset for the victim customer.

threats.title: Export API parameter abuse to generate exports of other customers' records
threats.description: A malicious customer manipulates the customer identifier in an export request so that the Export Worker assembles an export for a different customer, if tenant scoping and authorization on the named customer parameter are not correctly enforced.
preconditions: Export requests include a customer identifier and date range supplied by the requester (established: export requests name a customer and a date range; evd-003).

The Export API and Export Worker rely on the request-supplied customer identifier when selecting which customer records to include in the export (inferred from the worker assembling exports from customer records based on the request; evd-002, evd-003).
Authorization is not strictly enforced to ensure that the authenticated requester is allowed to access the named customer's records, or that check can be bypassed.
attack_path: A malicious customer authenticates and submits an export request over the public HTTPS Export API, but sets the "customer" parameter to identify a different target customer (evd-001, evd-002, evd-003, evd-004).
The Export API accepts the request and forwards it to the internal Export Worker to assemble the export (df-002; evd-001, evd-002).
The Export Worker queries customer records using the supplied customer identifier and assembles an export for the targeted customer instead of the attacker (evd-002, evd-003).
The resulting export file is written to the managed object store and made available for download, allowing the attacker to retrieve another customer's records (evd-003).
threats.impact: The attacker receives an export containing another customer's records for the specified date range, compromising confidentiality and violating tenant isolation guarantees.

threats.title: Bulk compromise of stored export files via managed object store or credential breach
threats.description: An attacker who gains read access to the managed object store or its credentials can list and download up to 30 days of stored export files for many customers, leading to large-scale disclosure of customer records.
preconditions: Completed export files are written to a managed object store and retained there under a storage lifecycle policy (evd-003, evd-006).
The storage lifecycle policy retains export objects for 30 days before expiring them, meaning many customers’ exports are present at any given time (evd-006).
An attacker is able to obtain read access to the managed object store (for example, via compromised credentials, misconfiguration, or provider-level compromise).
attack_path: The Export Worker writes completed export files, each containing a customer's records for a requested date range, to the managed object store (evd-002, evd-003).
The storage lifecycle policy retains these export objects for 30 days, accumulating a rolling window of recent exports (evd-006).
An attacker with access to the object store or its credentials lists export objects and enumerates identifiers for many customers.
The attacker downloads stored export files in bulk, obtaining historical customer records across multiple customers and date ranges.
threats.impact: A large volume of sensitive customer records from many customers is exposed at once, far beyond what would be available through a single export operation, significantly amplifying the confidentiality impact of any storage-layer compromise.

threats.title: Operator misuse of export retrieval capability
threats.description: A malicious or compromised operator misuses the operational capability to retrieve recent exports from the managed object store, accessing customers' export files without a legitimate failed-download case.
preconditions: Operators have a documented capability to retrieve recent export files from the managed object store when customers report failed downloads (evd-006).

The mechanism that allows operators to retrieve exports permits them to specify which export to retrieve (for example, by customer and date range) and can be used for any export within the retention window.
Operator access control, segregation of duties, or audit may be insufficient to reliably prevent or detect retrievals that are not tied to legitimate customer-reported failures.
attack_path: An operator account is compromised or an operator decides to misuse their access.
Using the operational tooling or console that supports retrieval of recent exports from the managed object store, the operator selects exports for a target customer or a set of customers (evd-006).
The retrieval mechanism pulls the export files from the managed object store and makes them available to the operator.
The operator saves or exfiltrates the export files, disclosing customers' records outside authorized support workflows.
threats.impact: Customer export files, each containing detailed records for specific date ranges, are accessed and potentially exfiltrated by an operator outside of legitimate support scenarios, resulting in insider-driven confidentiality breaches.

threats.title: Interception or tampering of internal export traffic if inter-service communication lacks strong protection
threats.description: An attacker with access to the internal network intercepts or alters traffic between the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store if those internal flows are not strongly encrypted and authenticated, leading to disclosure or corruption of export data.
preconditions: The Export API triggers the internal Export Worker to assemble exports and the Export Worker writes completed export files to the managed object store over internal data flows (df-002, df-003; evd-001, evd-002, evd-003, evd-006).
Encryption and strong mutual authentication for df-002 and df-003 are absent, misconfigured, or can be bypassed (encryption in transit is documented as unknown for these internal flows).

An attacker has a foothold on the internal network path between the Export API and Export Worker or between the Export Worker and managed object store (for example, via a compromised host or network device).
attack_path: The Export API forwards export requests, which identify a customer and date range, to the Export Worker over an internal channel (df-002; evd-002, evd-003).
The Export Worker assembles exports from customer records and sends completed export files to the managed object store over another internal channel (df-003; evd-002, evd-003, evd-006).

An attacker with internal network access intercepts these flows, capturing export requests and export file contents in transit, or modifies them to alter which records are exported or to inject corrupted data.
Customers subsequently download exports that have been observed or modified by the attacker, or the attacker retains copies of intercepted export files.
threats.impact: Customer records included in export files may be disclosed to an attacker monitoring internal traffic, and exports delivered to customers may be silently corrupted or manipulated, undermining both confidentiality and integrity of the exported data.

threats.title: Abuse of the public Export API to exhaust worker and storage resources
threats.description: An attacker repeatedly triggers export generation through the public Export API, causing the Export Worker and managed object store to consume excessive compute and storage resources, degrading export availability for legitimate customers.
preconditions: The Export API is a public HTTPS service reachable by customers over the internet, and export requests cause the internal Export Worker to assemble exports from customer records (evd-001, evd-002, evd-003).
Each export request results in non-trivial processing by the Export Worker and creation of an export file written to the managed object store (evd-002, evd-003).
Rate limiting, quotas, or similar mechanisms that bound export frequency, size, or total concurrent jobs per customer or account are absent, weak, or can be bypassed.
Export files are retained for 30 days under a storage lifecycle policy, so large volumes of generated exports accumulate before expiry (evd-006).
attack_path: An attacker, using their own customer account or compromised accounts, scripts a large number of export requests over the public HTTPS Export API (evd-001, evd-002).
The Export API accepts these requests and forwards them to the Export Worker, which begins assembling exports from customer records (df-002; evd-002, evd-003).
For each request, the Export Worker writes a completed export file to the managed object store, where it is retained for up to 30 days (df-003; evd-003, evd-006).

The sustained high volume of export processing and stored files consumes worker capacity and storage, causing legitimate customers' exports to be delayed, time out, or fail, and increasing operational load as reflected in monitoring metrics and alerts (evd-007).
threats.impact: Export generation and download for legitimate customers become slow, unreliable, or unavailable due to exhausted worker capacity and storage, and operational costs may increase from handling the excess load and storage consumption.
